verdicts.reason: Covert key/clipboard capture, browser-store deletion, image hollowing and UAC interference outweigh the remote-administration explanation. Operator authorization and deployment context are unavailable.
reverse_engineering: Rizin function analysis and annotated Capstone disassembly trace startup, configuration, hook recording, registry writes and image injection; no sample code was executed.
0x40a0e9 reads SETTINGS RT_RCDATA; 0x409c5e treats its first byte as key length, copies the key and decrypts the rest with RC4 routines 0x4031b3/0x40320d. The 418-byte resource uses a 149-byte key.

Decoded configuration contains remcoss.onmypc.org:3765, controller password, group/mutex, logs.dat, screenshot/audio locations and option fields. The endpoint corroborates configuration, not maliciousness by itself. Winlogon Shell selections (fields 6/7) are disabled; HKCU Run selection (field 4) is enabled. New Shell coverage describes included writer code, not observed/enabled Shell persistence.
0x405351 installs WH_KEYBOARD_LL with callback 0x405317. Recording paths coexist with clipboard reads at 0x406c16 and waveInOpen/waveInStart recording code at 0x401459/0x401472.
0x4032e9 builds the mscfile command hijack, writes through registry helpers, and launches eventvwr.exe. 0x40a4fc supplies the EnableLUA-zero command to CreateProcessA at 0x40a506.

0x407eb3 and 0x407f2b build comma-appended command strings, then pass the value name Shell and Winlogon key to 0x40ba71, which calls RegSetValueExW. The second prefix names userinit.exe, but the actual registry value is Shell. No new Userinit claim is made.

0x40f306 resolves NtUnmapViewOfSection; the same routine creates a suspended child, gets context, reads its image base, unmaps/replaces the image, writes remote memory, redirects context and resumes at 0x40f48e.

Browser-targeting routines starting at 0x407136 delete login/cookie stores. Generated VBS cleanup/update code uses DeleteFile(Wscript.ScriptFullName); the added notable rule describes the helper-script cleanup command, not native-image self-removal.
verdicts.changes: Added Winlogon Shell writer behavior and Remcos persistence identity composite, hostile keylogger/UAC interference combination, and embedded wide WSH helper self-deletion.
verdicts.remaining_context: Live C2 activity, task execution, enabled persistence and operator authorization are unknown. No runtime success is claimed.
verdicts.marker: Remcos RAT: covert logging and UAC bypass; add Shell/UAC coverage

verdicts.identification: Salat Stealer/RAT, unsigned Go 1.24.0 Windows/386 executable
verdicts.reason: Actual browser credential decryption, session collection, surveillance, remote tasking and interference with security controls establish an implant rather than an administrative utility.
reverse_engineering: go version -m identifies module salat and compiler/platform; PE has no Authenticode signature. Custom pclntab parsing recovered 10636 function boundaries; full annotated Capstone disassembly of the main package supports the conclusions.

getChromeLogins at 0x8f2dc0 opens the login database, queries rows and calls DecryptChrome. Steal at 0x8e5b30 invokes browser, Discord, Steam and screenshot acquisition, builds a ZIP, Base64-encodes it, JSON-marshals the result, transforms it through dec and calls rq.

The verified direct calls are Steal->rq at VA 0x8e8ae0, rq->tryRQ at 0x8d4a8e, tryRQ->net/http.NewRequestWithContext at 0x8d4dc0 and tryRQ->net/http.(*Client).do at 0x8d4ee4. New YARA resolves function names/ranges from pclntab and actual relative CALL targets; it does not pin these addresses.

runKeylogger at 0x8d1e30 opens the recording file and installs callbacks; keyPressCallback at 0x8d17e0 translates and writes keys through bufio.Writer. sendScreen at 0x8d2410 captures and encodes a screenshot, marshals it and calls rq.

tloop at 0x8e2280 parses controller tasks and calls doTask at 0x8e2890. The dispatcher includes downloads, command launching, data collection and status reporting. SOCKS/session helpers implement relay and interactive control.

staticinstall at 0x8da540 copies the image, calls newTask and writes a Run value. newTask at 0x8db580 builds timed task definitions and invokes CreateTask. getSystemToken at 0x8f9300 locates LSASS, opens its token and duplicates it for impersonation. selfDelete at 0x8fbad0 gets its image path and uses rename/disposition information through SetFileInformationByHandle.

At 0x8b7f1a main.init decodes the 1500-byte Base64 script at VA 0xa0cc94 into global 0xfc0490/494. main.main consumes that value, appends exit text and schedules main.main.gowrap3, which invokes shellCommand with powershell.exe. Decoded script adds Defender exclusions for Program Files and AppData, invokes reagentc /disable and sets EnableLUA to zero.
verdicts.changes: Added a neutral Go collector-to-HTTP call-chain matcher and hostile credential/surveillance upload composite. All prior theft, persistence, token, UAC, Defender, recovery and cleanup findings are retained.
verdicts.remaining_context: Deployment, live controller operation and command success are unknown. Bazaar/Triage URLs were inaccessible through the web tool. No sandbox-only assertions were added; static theft/control paths explain malware-corpus collection.
verdicts.marker: Salat RAT: steals credentials and uploads captures; add HTTP chain

verdicts.identification: Legacy RDS/ActiveX drive-by executable downloader HTML
verdicts.reason: Page-load code probes COM factories to bypass normal browser creation restrictions, downloads an executable, saves it and attempts ShellExecute without a user-driven installer workflow.
reverse_engineering: Read both scripts directly and reconstructed constant concatenations. Dead assignments add noise. CreateO evals six CreateObject/GetObject signature variants, suppressing errors; the outer loop probes 13 CLSIDs including RDS DataSpace, instantiates object elements and invokes Go for compatible factories.

Go constructs msxml2.XMLHTTP, synchronously GETs http://enterinmind.com/check/vers195.php?q=1, writes responseBody to an ADODB.Stream with type=1, saves an EXE with overwrite flag 2 and calls Shell.Application.ShellExecute on that same path.

The first function saves to .//..//ie_updates3r.exe after constant concatenation. Its return TRUE is an unresolved uppercase identifier in standalone JavaScript, but occurs after the ShellExecute attempt.

The fallback script tries an RDS-created ADODB.Stream and then direct ActiveXObject creation. It saves C:\ie_updater.exe. A stray standalone o after close() would raise ReferenceError before its ShellExecute in the supplied standalone context. This defect does not erase the first path or the saved-file behavior.

The new notable rule matches the concatenated ADODB.Stream ProgID. A suspicious composite requires the existing RDS downloader behavior, so an ordinary concatenated COM helper stays notable with no hostile/suspicious findings.
verdicts.changes: Preserved the existing hostile RDS save-and-launch detection and all other findings; added stream ProgID fragmentation and its suspicious downloader concealment combination.
verdicts.hostile_coverage_goal: One independently supported hostile chain remains. Factory probing, HTTP staging, stream saving and launch are parts of that exploit chain; adding three hostile aliases would duplicate it. Investigated both branches and obfuscation, added missing concealment coverage, and tested save-only/no-launch controls. No additional independent hostile behavior or final payload bytes are available.
verdicts.remaining_context: Final downloaded payload, page hosting context, installed/vulnerable controls and runtime success are unknown. No final malware family or exact exploit CVE is inferred.
verdicts.marker: RDS downloader: fetches and launches EXE; add ProgID concealment

testing.controls: Keep all names while removing collector->request or helper->HTTP-send CALL; redirect Winlogon prefix operands; change UAC zero to one; remove helper-script self path; rename endpoint; remove launches; ordinary COM helper; pre-existing RDS positive and save-only fixtures.

classifier_review: Both native samples alert before and after. The initial HTML scan exited 0 at confidence 49/level 7500 despite its hostile RDS trait; after accurate concealment coverage it exits 1 and terminal output is HOSTILE[100%], confidence 100/level 0. Thus no disagreement remains at the default alert gate. Model feature spec v18 is older than engine v21; no rules were changed to optimize scores.
rule_changes: Eight new YAML files, eight new detections; no existing matcher, severity or exception was weakened or removed. Four neutral observations, three hostile behavior/identity composites and one suspicious concealment composite.
